rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> two field experiments in 'Fuji'/M9 and 'Fuji'/M26 orchards at Wanju, Korea, with sprinkler, surface drip and subsurface drip treatments in three replications, irrigation water measured by flow meter. Q2: Abstract and Results Exp I, Table 2 <U+2013> subsurface drip used 188.1 vs 258.4 (surface drip) and 299.7 (sprinkler) Mg/10a to hold the same matric potential, i.e. about 37% and 27% less; Exp II, Table 5 <U+2013> 30 cm subsurface drip used 138.4 vs 288.2 Mg/10a for surface drip, significantly less. Q8: Conclusions <U+2013> authors state results are for a single growing season and following years' data are needed to understand efficiency of the systems. Q9: Table 5 <U+2013> irrigation water reported as mean <U+00B1> SE (288.2<U+00B1>33.8, 167.2<U+00B1>34.8, 138.4<U+00B1>25.3 Mg/10a); Table 3/5 footnotes state means of three replications <U+00B1> SE.
rows.notes: Single method (flow meter) so no triangulation. Tensiometer matric potential was the control criterion, not a measured mechanism of water saving (no evaporation or soil water balance measured). One site, one crop (two rootstocks), plot scale. Burial depth (30 cm) was found to matter but is not stated as a requirement. Note Table 2 (Exp I) shows no significant difference in irrigation water between methods (all letter 'a') and no SE is printed for that column; significance of the water saving is only shown in Exp II (Table 5). Text gives 14% saving for surface drip vs sprinkler, 37% for subsurface vs sprinkler.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own field experiment with sprinkler, surface drip and subsurface drip treatments in three replications; weed amount determined per 1 m3 in each treatment. Q2: Results Exp I, Table 3 <U+2013> subsurface drip had significantly lower weed amount (20.7 Mg/10a) than sprinkler (24.5) and surface drip (23.7); Conclusions state subsurface drip can decrease weed growth. Q8: Conclusions <U+2013> results presented are for a single growing season; data from following years needed. Q9: Table 3 <U+2013> weed growth reported as mean <U+00B1> SE (24.5<U+00B1>0.37, 23.7<U+00B1>0.32, 20.7<U+00B1>0.41 Mg/10a).
rows.notes: Weed reduction is reported only for subsurface drip in Exp I, one site, one crop, plot scale, single method; no intermediate variable (e.g. surface soil wetting) measured. Methods state weed growth was 'controlled' during the growing season, which makes the weed measurement procedure unclear. Weed amounts differ modestly (about 15%) and the Exp I design has one replicate block per row.

notes: Full text available. Short two-year establishment trial of young apple trees in Korea; water data are for March<U+2013>October 2018 only. Abstract figures (37% and 27%) correspond to Table 2 in which treatment means for irrigation water are not statistically different; the significant water saving appears in Exp II (Table 5) comparing burial depths.
